title: NATIVE: Nanobody-assisted tissue immunostaining for volumetric EM
protocol: Weigh the mouse and calculate the anesthetic dosage (100 mg/kg sodium pentobarbital).
Administer the anesthetic via intraperitoneal injection.
After complete anesthesia is achieved, secure the mouse ventral side up in the dissecting pan.
Cut the chest through the sternum and pin open the ribcage to expose the heart.
Make a small incision to the left ventricle.
Insert the blunt needle through the cut into the ascending aorta and clamp it to the left ventricle.
Immediately cut the right atrium and start the infusion of carbonated aCSF at 10 mL/min.
Turn off the pump after the fluid exiting the heart becomes clear, typically after about 15 mL buffer.
Switch the tubing from aCSF to ice-cold PFA fixative without introducing any bubbles.
Start the pump and perfuse about 30 mL PFA fixative.
Carefully remove the brain from the skull and place it in a vial of fresh PFA fixative on ice.
Trim the brain if necessary and mount it on the vibratome stage with Krazy Glue.
Fill the buffer tray with ice-cold PFA fixative to submerge the brain.
Cut 120 µm-thick brain slices in the desired plane with the vibratome.
Transfer the slices into fresh PFA fixative solution.
Fix for 24 hours with gentle agitation at 4 °C.
Trim the PFA fixed brain slices into smaller pieces containing the target area.
Transfer trimmed tissue sections to a clean 24-well plate.
Rinse the tissue sections 3 times in PBS, each for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Add glycine blocking solution and wait for 20 minutes.
Remove the blocking solution.
Add 1 mL of nanobody staining solution to each well.
Wrap the well plate with aluminum foil.
Incubate for 48 hours at 4 °C with gentle agitation.
Rinse the tissue sections 3 times in PBS, each for 5 minutes at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Stain nuclei with Hoechst staining solution for 5 hours at 4 °C.
Rinse the tissue sections 3 times in PBS, each for 5 minutes at room temperature with gentle agitation.
Apply a 120 µm secure-seal spacer onto a clean glass coverslip.
Transfer the tissue section to the well using a brush and add an appropriate amount of PBS to prevent drying.
Put another coverslip on top to seal the tissue.
Perform fluorescence imaging on a Zeiss LSM 880 confocal laser scanning microscope equipped with a 40x/1.3 NA oil-objective lens.
Take a low resolution image of the entire sample after imaging.
Mark regions imaged in high resolution in the low-res image.
Gently separate the two coverslips.
Remove the imaged tissue with a brush and immediately transfer it to ice-cold glutaraldehyde fixative for post-fixation overnight at 4 °C.
Rinse the sample 3 times, each for 5 min, in 150 mM sodium cacodylate buffer at room temperature.
Stain the sample in a solution containing 1% w/v OsO4, 1.5% w/v K4Fe(CN)6 and 150 mM sodium cacodylate at room temperature for 1 hour.
Rinse the sample 3 times, each for 5 min, with distilled water.
Incubate the sample in filtered 1% w/v TCH aqueous solution in a 40 °C oven for 30 min.
Wash the sample 3 times, each for 5 min, with distilled water.
Stain the tissue with 2% OsO4 aqueous solution at room temperature for 1 hour.
Rinse the sample 3 times for 5 minutes each with dH₂O.
Transfer the sample to a 1% uranyl acetate aqueous solution.
Incubate the sample in the uranyl acetate solution at 4°C overnight, protected from light.
Incubate the sample in the uranyl acetate solution at 50°C for 1 hour.
Rinse the sample 3 times for 5 minutes each with dH₂O.
Dehydrate the sample through a graded acetonitrile series (25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%) for 5 minutes each, followed by anhydrous acetonitrile for 10 minutes.
Infiltrate the sample with 25% EPON:acetonitrile for 1 hour.
Infiltrate the sample with 50% EPON:acetonitrile for 2 hours.
Infiltrate the sample with 75% EPON:acetonitrile for 3 hours.
Infiltrate the sample with 100% EPON overnight on a rotator.
Transfer the resin-infiltrated sample to an embedding capsule and incubate in fresh EPON at 60°C for two days.
Trim the block face of the sample cylinder into a 1.5 x 1.5 mm square containing the region of interest imaged by light microscopy.
Cut 50 nm serial ultrathin sections using a Leica ultramicrotome and collect on a home-built automated tape collecting system on carbon-coated and plasma-treated Kapton tape.
After collection, cut the tape into strips with appropriate lengths and mount them onto 100 mm silicon wafers using double-sided conductive sticky tape.
Image the sections with a scanning electron microscope.
Use a Zeiss Sigma SEM with a backscattered electron detector and a Fibics imaging system.
Take a few images of full sections at low resolution in SEM (50 nm per pixel).
Compare low-resolution SEM images with light microscopy images to find regions of interest.
Locate the layer of granule cell bodies of the dentate gyrus and pyramidal cell bodies of CA3 using light microscopy images.
Use blood vessels with characteristic shapes as fiducial markers to pinpoint the region of interest.
Draw the regions of interest in each section.
Set up an imaging workflow using the Zeiss Atlas 5 software.
Acquire high-resolution serial images of the ROIs (12k x 12k pixel image, 5 nm per pixel) with a working distance of ~7.3 mm, 8 keV incident electron energy, and a dwell time of 2 µs.
Align the EM image stack with Fiji using the "Linear Stack Alignment with SIFT" plugin.
Load LM images into VAST separately.
Load aligned EM images into VAST separately.
Identify characteristic features visible in both image stacks, including nucleoli, blood vessel branch points, and lysosomes.
Record coordinates for each feature in both the EM and LM stack by placing dots in VAST.
Export point coordinates from VAST.
Analyze exported coordinates in Matlab.
Compute a three-dimensional affine transformation using the set of corresponding-point pairs to match EM points to LM points via least-squares method.
Use the computed affine transformation to translate LM image stacks into the EM coordinate system.
For each pixel in the EM-aligned LM stack, transform its coordinates to the corresponding location in the LM stack and copy the LM color.
Optionally perform the process at a lower resolution for speed and upsample the resulting images to full resolution if necessary.
Save the transformed LM images.
Import transformed LM images into VAST.
Display both stacks together in VAST.
Load large image stacks into VAST for visualization.
Manually label microglia, astrocyte, and blood vessel endothelial cell in each cross-section using a label color.
Export the surfaces of labeled voxel objects as surface meshes using VastTools script in Matlab.
Save exported surface meshes as Wavefront .obj files.
Load mesh files into 3D animation software 3ds Max.
Set up colors, shading, lighting, and camera in 3ds Max.
Render images and videos from the set-up scene.
